CannonBalls.EnglishDescription: Standard cannonballs that deal damage across the full range of your Guns. They throw off a great many splinters on impact

Shells filled with an incendiary mixture. They deal #more #damage by setting ships ablaze and leaving behind a burning area. They can detonate Barrels floating in the water. Effective against ships with high Defense and groups of enemies
Two half-balls joined by a chain to do maximum damage to #sails and rigging. They #lower the enemy’s #speed and #maneuverability, and can destroy Guns on the enemy ship.

Deals heavy crew damage and reloads fast. #Outnumbering the enemy crew improves your odds #in #boarding, and a big advantage lets you take captives with fewer losses. Damage to sailors slows #reloading.
Unique Imperial shot. The best thing you can fire from a cannon at the enemy. Reloads slower, but hits harder.
Mortar ammunition. Deals area damage–the closer to the epicenter, the more damage. A good choice against clustered enemies and shore structures.
Costly shot “stuffed” with white Bengal fire powder. It can #pierce a hull #clean #through, damaging several ships at once. Obtainable during events, from Imperial Flagships’ holds, or in the Store.
Mortar ammunition. Deals area damage–the closer to the epicenter, the more damage. Especially effective against sails and crew. Drawback: shorter range.
Ammunition for #Swivel #Guns. Long firing range and low cost are its main advantages.
Ammunition for #Swivel #Guns. Fires on an arcing trajectory, hitting targets behind obstacles.
Ammunition for #Swivel #Guns. Excellent area damage and increased damage to sails.
Ammunition for #Swivel #Guns. No celebration is complete without them, and any day can be a celebration. The enemy crew will appreciate them most.
Round shot made of packed snow. For unknown reasons, it deals damage only to the Sea Elves–strange vessels that entered the Archipelago’s waters on Christmas Eve.

ShipsToPlay.EnglishDescription: A classic topsail schooner with light armament. She became famous for carrying the news of Nelson’s victory at Trafalgar to England. Why do new captains arrive in the Archipelago aboard this very schooner?...
ShipsToPlay.ConstructionDataStatus: See Ship_Construction; some costs depend on model gun ports

ShipsToPlay.EnglishDescription: “Red Seal Ship”: such ships were used by the Tokugawa shogunate for trade and diplomatic missions to Southeast Asian ports. Upon reaching the Archipelago, she was converted into an excellent warship.
ShipsToPlay.ConstructionDataStatus: See Ship_Construction; some costs depend on model gun ports

ShipsToPlay.EnglishDescription: Built in 1752 in Toulon, she was successfully used to bombard Barbary pirate bases in Algiers
ShipsToPlay.ConstructionDataStatus: See Ship_Construction; some costs depend on model gun ports

ShipsToPlay.EnglishDescription: The Venetian fleet kept armed polaccas in service to protect trade routes in the Adriatic Sea from Dalmatian, Greek, and Turkish pirates
ShipsToPlay.ConstructionDataStatus: See Ship_Construction; some costs depend on model gun ports

ShipsToPlay.EnglishDescription: The brigantine won fame among pirates for her seaworthiness, maneuverability, and speed. Even the name took on a new meaning–literally a “brigand’s ship” (Italian brigante means “brigand, pirate”).
ShipsToPlay.ConstructionDataStatus: See Ship_Construction; some costs depend on model gun ports

ShipsToPlay.EnglishDescription: First built by Maurice “the Shipwright” Fleury in the port of Aruba. Through the intrigues of the Levenhook brothers, Maurice fell into a trap and was cruelly executed. In the Shipwright’s memory, the bow bears a skeleton with a cup–a symbol of grief drunk to the dregs–and a spear–a symbol of revenge.
ShipsToPlay.ConstructionDataStatus: See Ship_Construction; some costs depend on model gun ports

ShipsToPlay.EnglishDescription: The first two of these ships were spotted near Gray Island, crewed by Russian sailors and officers who had fled the Tsar’s rule in search of a new, free life
ShipsToPlay.ConstructionDataStatus: See Ship_Construction; some costs depend on model gun ports

ShipsToPlay.EnglishDescription: These clumsy but reliable ships plied between the New and Old Worlds for 200 years, carrying cargo and valuables, including gold from South America to Spain. They became tempting prey for pirates and gave rise to the long rivalry of brigantines and galleons.
ShipsToPlay.ConstructionDataStatus: See Ship_Construction; some costs depend on model gun ports

ShipsToPlay.EnglishDescription: A sailing frigate of the Russian Empire, laid down in 1724 under Peter the Great by master shipwright Browne and launched in 1728. She fought in two wars, and in 1734, during the blockade of Danzig, captured the French 30-gun frigate “Le Brilliant”
ShipsToPlay.ConstructionDataStatus: See Ship_Construction; some costs depend on model gun ports

ShipsToPlay.EnglishDescription: A heavily armed American frigate. She fought in the First Barbary War and the War of 1812, during which she captured 13 whalers on a single cruise. Later captured by the British, the “Essex” went on to serve the British Crown.
ShipsToPlay.ConstructionDataStatus: See Ship_Construction; some costs depend on model gun ports

ShipsToPlay.EnglishDescription: The battle galleon of the pirate prince Morgan Black, said to have been granted to him by the Empire for his service. One of the best-armed ships of her rate.
ShipsToPlay.ConstructionDataStatus: See Ship_Construction; some costs depend on model gun ports

ShipsToPlay.EnglishDescription: Tartanes were widely used across the Mediterranean–from Turkey to Spain–for a variety of tasks. They were especially favored by Algerian corsairs. Upon reaching the Archipelago, the tartane became popular with local pirates, particularly after Tortuga craftsmen fitted it with Mortars.
ShipsToPlay.ConstructionDataStatus: See Ship_Construction; some costs depend on model gun ports

ShipsToPlay.EnglishDescription: The “Devourer” is an Imperial ship with heavy armament at both bow and stern. Her thick hull gives excellent Defense, and her jibs good maneuverability.
ShipsToPlay.ConstructionDataStatus: See Ship_Construction; some costs depend on model gun ports

ShipsToPlay.EnglishDescription: A revolutionary Dutch ship of the late 16th century, designed to make transoceanic voyages easier with maximum hold space and crew efficiency. Fluyts gave Dutch merchants a competitive edge and helped the Netherlands become a great sea power.
ShipsToPlay.ConstructionDataStatus: See Ship_Construction; some costs depend on model gun ports

ShipsToPlay.EnglishDescription: Fine lightweight timber gives this refitted battle schooner excellent sailing qualities and maneuverability. Pirates once took the bait of her showy looks, thinking some wealthy person was aboard. It turned out to be an ambush.
ShipsToPlay.ConstructionDataStatus: See Ship_Construction; some costs depend on model gun ports

ShipsToPlay.EnglishDescription: Originally built for trade voyages and supplying towns with provisions, thanks to her huge hold. Yet she can hold her own in battle. She gained a grim reputation as a slave ship from Africa to America.
ShipsToPlay.ConstructionDataStatus: See Ship_Construction; some costs depend on model gun ports

ShipsToPlay.EnglishDescription: Originally a Dutch fluyt, she was heavily reworked after arriving in the Archipelago. Many still mistake her for the lightly armed “Friede,” only to realize their fatal error too late, when Mortar shells smash their decks to splinters.
ShipsToPlay.ConstructionDataStatus: See Ship_Construction; some costs depend on model gun ports

ShipsToPlay.EnglishDescription: A warship with an impressive service record. She fought at the Battle of the Saintes on April 9, 1782, under Admiral Sir George Rodney against Admiral de Grasse. In 1794, she was rebuilt as a large 44-gun frigate and later took part in the Revolutionary and Napoleonic wars.
ShipsToPlay.ConstructionDataStatus: See Ship_Construction; some costs depend on model gun ports

ShipsToPlay.EnglishDescription: A 17th-century East Indiaman of the Dutch East India Company and the largest ship in its fleet. Her maiden voyage to the Dutch East Indies was in 1651. After several voyages, she sank near Madagascar in 1662. Fortunately, her plans are still in the hands of local shipwrights.
ShipsToPlay.ConstructionDataStatus: See Ship_Construction; some costs depend on model gun ports

ShipsToPlay.EnglishDescription: The “Black Wind’s” thick, sturdy hull and large crew provide solid Defense, but the price is a small hold for goods or ammunition
ShipsToPlay.ConstructionDataStatus: See Ship_Construction; some costs depend on model gun ports

ShipsToPlay.EnglishDescription: Originally the Korean “turtle ship,” with an enclosed, protected hull. The first such ships fought the Japanese fleet at the Battle of Noryang. Improved by local shipwrights.
ShipsToPlay.ConstructionDataStatus: See Ship_Construction; some costs depend on model gun ports

ShipsToPlay.EnglishDescription: A light and very fast French Navy corvette with fairly strong armament. She took part in the Franco-Mexican War and the bombardment of Fort San Juan de Ulúa near Veracruz.
ShipsToPlay.ConstructionDataStatus: See Ship_Construction; some costs depend on model gun ports

ShipsToPlay.EnglishDescription: This heavy U.S. Navy frigate was larger, better armed, and better built than standard frigates of her day. She distinguished herself in the War of 1812 against Great Britain, earning the nickname “Old Ironsides” and the public’s adoration.
ShipsToPlay.ConstructionDataStatus: See Ship_Construction; some costs depend on model gun ports

ShipsToPlay.EnglishDescription: The main warship of the Kai fleet. Fearsome in appearance, with a sturdy hull, mixed armament, and Mortars, she can fight in any conditions.
ShipsToPlay.ConstructionDataStatus: See Ship_Construction; some costs depend on model gun ports

ShipsToPlay.EnglishDescription: Launched on March 2, 1779, at Saint-Malo, she patrolled the coast of Brittany and fought her first battle against two English cutters on June 21 of that year. She became famous for her elusiveness.
ShipsToPlay.ConstructionDataStatus: See Ship_Construction; some costs depend on model gun ports

ShipsToPlay.EnglishDescription: With a fearsome appearance, powerful armament, a strong hull, and a large cargo hold, the “Firestorm” became a legendary Imperial ship. The first “Firestorms” were captured and studied after Longhorn’s victory over the Immortal Admirals.
ShipsToPlay.ConstructionDataStatus: See Ship_Construction; some costs depend on model gun ports
See Ship_Construction; some costs depend on model gun ports

ShipsToPlay.EnglishDescription: The flagship of Horatio Nelson, one of the greatest and largest warships of the British Royal Navy, immortalized at the Battle of Trafalgar. Launched in 1765, she remains the oldest commissioned warship in the world with 245 years of service as of 2023.
ShipsToPlay.ConstructionDataStatus: See Ship_Construction; some costs depend on model gun ports

ShipsToPlay.EnglishDescription: A French ship of the line from the late 17th century. Launched in 1691, she fought in the War of the League of Augsburg. During the War of the Spanish Succession (1701–1713), she was captured by the English and wrecked in Vigo Bay in 1702.
ShipsToPlay.ConstructionDataStatus: See Ship_Construction; some costs depend on model gun ports
See Ship_Construction; some costs depend on model gun ports

ShipsToPlay.EnglishDescription: Clippers have the most powerful sail plan and a unique hull shape that minimizes drag at the cost of maneuverability. This ship held the record for the fastest passage from New York to San Francisco: 89 days and 8 hours.
ShipsToPlay.ConstructionDataStatus: See Ship_Construction; some costs depend on model gun ports

ShipsToPlay.EnglishDescription: These Imperial ships were first used at the Battle of Devios as part of the “Iron Squadron.” Unwieldy, heavily armored, and powerfully armed, they withstood the blow of Hispaniola’s fleet. Ever since, the battle site has been known as Lágrimas de Viudas–the Sea of Widows’ Tears.
ShipsToPlay.ConstructionDataStatus: See Ship_Construction; some costs depend on model gun ports

ShipsToPlay.EnglishDescription: The largest Spanish ship of the line, which fought at the Battle of Trafalgar. She has her weak points–heavy and unwieldy–but can easily devastate both shore fortifications and whole squadrons of enemy frigates.
ShipsToPlay.ConstructionDataStatus: See Ship_Construction; some costs depend on model gun ports

ShipsToPlay.EnglishDescription: A glorious ship of the line of the Black Sea Fleet that saw many battles. From 1784 to 1788, her captain was F. F. Ushakov, the future legendary Russian admiral.
ShipsToPlay.ConstructionDataStatus: See Ship_Construction; some costs depend on model gun ports

ShipsToPlay.EnglishDescription: Originally a 17th-century Spanish Manila galleon: such heavily armed galleons carried Spanish treasure from the Philippines to Mexico. After arriving in the Archipelago, she was improved and won wide fame.
ShipsToPlay.ConstructionDataStatus: See Ship_Construction; some costs depend on model gun ports

ShipsToPlay.EnglishDescription: The “turtle ship” was the core of the Korean fleet in the 16th and 17th centuries. Besides her unique covered design, she carries mixed armament, including Mortars.
ShipsToPlay.ConstructionDataStatus: See Ship_Construction; some costs depend on model gun ports

ShipsToPlay.EnglishDescription: Originally a French ship of the line, she was captured by the English at the “Glorious First of June” in 1794. She served actively in the Royal Navy until 1807, fighting in a number of actions and taking several ships. In 1807, she was converted into a prison ship.
ShipsToPlay.ConstructionDataStatus: See Ship_Construction; some costs depend on model gun ports

ShipsToPlay.EnglishDescription: One of the fastest and best-armed ships of her rate, making her a dangerous opponent for medium frigates
ShipsToPlay.ConstructionDataStatus: See Ship_Construction; some costs depend on model gun ports

ShipsToPlay.EnglishDescription: The first ship of the line approved after Lord Anson became First Lord of the Admiralty. She took part in the Seven Years’ War, the American War of Independence, and the Napoleonic Wars.
ShipsToPlay.ConstructionDataStatus: See Ship_Construction; some costs depend on model gun ports

ShipsToPlay.EnglishDescription: A British ship of the line that served as a model for the largest warships of the 17th century. The most powerful ship of her day, she was overloaded with guns and had poor stability.
ShipsToPlay.ConstructionDataStatus: See Ship_Construction; some costs depend on model gun ports

ShipsToPlay.EnglishDescription: French frigates and naval sloops did poorly against the Barbary pirates in their nimble xebecs. It was only logical to use xebecs against them too. The Requin–“Shark” in French–was launched in 1751 in Toulon and made the pirates’ lives much harder.
ShipsToPlay.ConstructionDataStatus: See Ship_Construction; some costs depend on model gun ports
See Ship_Construction; some costs depend on model gun ports

ShipsToPlay.EnglishDescription: The first ship of the line of the French Navy, “La Couronne” was laid down at the La Roche-Bernard shipyard in 1629 at the personal initiative of Cardinal Richelieu. She was the flagship at the Battle of Guetaria, where the new French fleet defeated a Spanish squadron.
ShipsToPlay.ConstructionDataStatus: See Ship_Construction; some costs depend on model gun ports

ShipsToPlay.EnglishDescription: A warship of the Russian Empire’s Baltic Fleet, designed by Peter the Great: the first of her class and one of the Tsar’s favorite ships. In the Great Northern War, she was the flagship of both the Russian fleet and the combined Russo-Danish-Dutch-English fleet, at times sailing under Peter’s personal standard.
ShipsToPlay.ConstructionDataStatus: See Ship_Construction; some costs depend on model gun ports
See Ship_Construction; some costs depend on model gun ports

ShipsToPlay.EnglishDescription: A famed French ship of the line that dueled with HMS Victory at the Battle of Trafalgar. The shot that killed Vice-Admiral Horatio Nelson was fired from this very ship.
ShipsToPlay.ConstructionDataStatus: See Ship_Construction; some costs depend on model gun ports

ShipsToPlay.EnglishDescription: Built in 1681 with private funds by Charles Mordaunt, Earl of Peterborough, and named after him. She was too heavily armed for a private vessel, so she was confiscated in 1683 and later, after legal battles, bought by the Royal Navy.
ShipsToPlay.ConstructionDataStatus: See Ship_Construction; some costs depend on model gun ports

ShipsToPlay.EnglishDescription: The oared frigate of William Kidd, the pirate hunter who turned pirate himself. First launched in 1695, she sailed thousands of miles across the Atlantic and Indian Oceans.
ShipsToPlay.ConstructionDataStatus: See Ship_Construction; some costs depend on model gun ports

ShipsToPlay.EnglishDescription: A ship of the line of the Black Sea Fleet, she took part in the defense of Sevastopol during the Crimean War. She was scuttled with other ships on February 13, 1855, to block Anglo-French ships from entering the harbor. Fortunately, the Archipelago’s shipwrights managed to recover her plans.
ShipsToPlay.ConstructionDataStatus: See Ship_Construction; some costs depend on model gun ports

ShipsToPlay.EnglishDescription: A marvelous invention of 1783. You can control altitude, speed, and direction, but you can’t fly against the wind. The balloon can be shot at and may crash into mountains.
ShipsToPlay.ConstructionDataStatus: See Ship_Construction; some costs depend on model gun ports

ShipsToPlay.EnglishDescription: Named after the victory over the Swedish Empire at Poltava, she was the first ship of the line laid down and built at the Saint Petersburg Admiralty. She has a “Dutch” transom and is decorated with carvings of Saint George.
ShipsToPlay.ConstructionDataStatus: See Ship_Construction; some costs depend on model gun ports

ShipsToPlay.EnglishDescription: The French ship Unité combined the traits of a corvette and a light frigate, with phenomenal speed and maneuverability. After her capture by the British, she became the legendary HMS Surprise, the model for Patrick O’Brian’s novels and the film “Master and Commander”
ShipsToPlay.ConstructionDataStatus: See Ship_Construction; some costs depend on model gun ports

ShipsToPlay.EnglishDescription: The flagship of the Duke of Medina Sidonia, commander of the Spanish Armada. First launched in 1580, she played a crucial role in defending the Armada as she sailed through the English Channel. She survived the storm and English cannons to return safely to Spain.
ShipsToPlay.ConstructionDataStatus: See Ship_Construction; some costs depend on model gun ports

ShipsToPlay.EnglishDescription: A French galleass from the late 17th century. Based on the traditional Mediterranean galley, but built on a larger scale.
ShipsToPlay.ConstructionDataStatus: See Ship_Construction; some costs depend on model gun ports

ShipsToPlay.EnglishDescription: The flagship of Dutch Admiral de Ruyter, launched in 1665. A veteran of many victorious naval battles, the ship was named in honor of the seven autonomous provinces that formed the Dutch Republic in the 17th century.
ShipsToPlay.ConstructionDataStatus: See Ship_Construction; some costs depend on model gun ports

ShipsToPlay.EnglishDescription: A warship built on the Empire’s slipways. She was first captured in a battle with the Cult of the Witnesses of the Apocalypse. Before he died, the cultists’ captain revealed that such ships had been found drifting without crews somewhere in the Endless Sea.
ShipsToPlay.ConstructionDataStatus: See Ship_Construction; some costs depend on model gun ports

ShipsToPlay.EnglishDescription: A paddle-wheel sailing steamer found stuck in the ice in the north of the Archipelago. No survivors were found, so how she got here remains a mystery... Revolutionary as she is, her inefficient, oversized steam engine burns a lot of coal and takes up space, leaving the ship lightly armed and ill-suited to harsh conditions.
ShipsToPlay.ConstructionDataStatus: See Ship_Construction; some costs depend on model gun ports
See Ship_Construction; some costs depend on model gun ports

ShipsToPlay.EnglishDescription: Named after Huracan, the Maya god of wind, this giant is a symbol of the military might of the Inhagger Empire, a Native American civilization whose technology equals that of the Archipelago states and in many ways surpasses it
ShipsToPlay.ConstructionDataStatus: See Ship_Construction; some costs depend on model gun ports
See Ship_Construction; some costs depend on model gun ports

ShipsToPlay.EnglishDescription: A German “great” frigate of the 17th century. On July 25, 1692, the Friedrich Wilhelm sailed with the fleet from Emden for Guinea and was caught in a storm. When the storm died down, the crew saw an unknown shore. So she ended up in the Archipelago, where Hispaniola captured her.
ShipsToPlay.ConstructionDataStatus: See Ship_Construction; some costs depend on model gun ports

ShipsToPlay.EnglishDescription: A ship of the line ordered by Cardinal Richelieu as part of a shipbuilding program to strengthen the French navy. She fought in several battles and finally burned at the Battle of La Hougue after an attack by English fire ships.
ShipsToPlay.ConstructionDataStatus: See Ship_Construction; some costs depend on model gun ports

ShipsToPlay.EnglishDescription: Flagship of the Black Sea Fleet, hero of the Battle of Navarino. The first Russian ship awarded the St. George stern flag for victory over five Turkish ships.
ShipsToPlay.ConstructionDataStatus: See Ship_Construction; some costs depend on model gun ports

ShipsToPlay.EnglishDescription: A ship meant to be the pride of the Swedish Empire that instead became famous for sinking on her maiden voyage. Severian shipwrights fixed her design flaws and built a copy that will win glory in battle.
ShipsToPlay.ConstructionDataStatus: See Ship_Construction; some costs depend on model gun ports

ShipsToPlay.EnglishDescription: A Norwegian gunboat schooner, one of ten built for the Dano-Norwegian fleet before the end of the Napoleonic Wars, when Norway became independent of Denmark under the Treaty of Kiel in 1814.
ShipsToPlay.ConstructionDataStatus: See Ship_Construction; some costs depend on model gun ports

ShipsToPlay.EnglishDescription: This frigate served in the fleet for over 55 years, taking part in both military operations and delicate diplomatic missions, including carrying members of the royal family. The Southampton became the prototype of the 32-gun frigate class of the same name, which played an important role in the British fleet in the late 18th century.
ShipsToPlay.ConstructionDataStatus: See Ship_Construction; some costs depend on model gun ports

ShipsToPlay.EnglishDescription: One of the firstborn of Hispaniola’s shipbuilding school. This frigate type was first laid down at the San Martinas shipyard. Widely used for patrols, guarding trade routes from pirates, and raids deep into enemy territory.
ShipsToPlay.ConstructionDataStatus: See Ship_Construction; some costs depend on model gun ports

ShipsToPlay.EnglishDescription: This ship belonged to the large and successful “Slava Rossii” class of ships of the line (built from 1733 to 1774 in St. Petersburg and Arkhangelsk; 58 vessels in total), known for their seaworthiness, maneuverability, and stability. “Three Hierarchs” was one of the key ships of the first major ocean expedition of the Russian fleet from the Baltic to the Mediterranean, and a symbol of the Chesme victory.
ShipsToPlay.ConstructionDataStatus: See Ship_Construction; some costs depend on model gun ports

ShipsToPlay.EnglishDescription: This ship was paid for by the people of Cantabria (the “mountain” region of Spain, hence the name Montañés, “the Highlander”). She set the standard for later Spanish 74-gun ships of the line of the late 18th century and took part in almost every major naval engagement from the late 18th to the early 19th century.
ShipsToPlay.ConstructionDataStatus: See Ship_Construction; some costs depend on model gun ports
See Ship_Construction; some costs depend on model gun ports

ShipsToPlay.EnglishDescription: The famous British 50-gun ship of the Portland class. Launched on April 24, 1790, at Portsmouth. She became a symbol of British naval supremacy after the incident with the frigate Chesapeake. A reliable veteran of the Napoleonic Wars, able to hold out in a long duel. She met her end on June 28, 1814, wrecked in thick fog off Anticosti Island in the Gulf of St. Lawrence.
ShipsToPlay.ConstructionDataStatus: See Ship_Construction; some costs depend on model gun ports

ShipsToPlay.EnglishDescription: Originally the French East Indiaman Duc de Duras, launched in 1765. In 1779, she was transferred to John Paul Jones and renamed Bonhomme Richard in honor of Benjamin Franklin. She became famous for her victory over HMS Serapis in a fierce boarding action. Heavily damaged during the battle, she sank in the North Sea on September 25, 1779.
ShipsToPlay.ConstructionDataStatus: See Ship_Construction; some costs depend on model gun ports

ShipsToPlay.EnglishDescription: The flagship of the Kai coastal fleet, designed to dominate straits and coastal waters. Multi-tiered superstructures with tiled roofs shelter marksmen, while 40 broadside guns make the ship a formidable opponent. Enemies nicknamed her “the fortress that sails.”
ShipsToPlay.ConstructionDataStatus: See Ship_Construction; some costs depend on model gun ports

ShipsToPlay.EnglishDescription: A medium warship of Kai, named after the Guardian Dragon of the East. The elegant design of a traditional junk is combined with European armament–18 broadside guns and 4 bow cannons. Faster than the heavy fortresses, stronger than light frigates. An ideal all-rounder for patrolling trade routes and escorting fleets.
ShipsToPlay.ConstructionDataStatus: See Ship_Construction; some costs depend on model gun ports

ShipsToPlay.EnglishDescription: A Spanish 70-gun ship of the line launched in 1765. She took part in some of the largest naval battles of the late 18th and early 19th centuries. She became famous at the Battle of Trafalgar (1805), where under the command of Cosme Damián de Churruca she fought to the last, losing nearly her entire crew. Captured by the British after the battle, she was commissioned into the Royal Navy and broken up in 1818.
ShipsToPlay.ConstructionDataStatus: See Ship_Construction; some costs depend on model gun ports

ShipsToPlay.EnglishDescription: A Baltic Fleet ship of the line, laid down in 1769 in St. Petersburg. She served in the Russo-Turkish War of 1768–1774: she made the passage to the Mediterranean and took part in the blockade of the Dardanelles. In 1778, she was converted into a 50-gun ship, and she was sold for scrap in 1780 after ten years of service.
ShipsToPlay.ConstructionDataStatus: See Ship_Construction; some costs depend on model gun ports

ShipsToPlay.EnglishDescription: A veteran frigate that lived through three decades of wars and revolutions. Launched at Mahon in 1792, when Europe had not yet heard of Napoleon. She fought off Cape St. Vincent, carried armies clear of the French, ferried troops across the Atlantic, and hunted smugglers. She saw the Spanish empire rise and fall. By the time she was broken up, the world was a different place, but Diana stayed loyal to her flag to the end.
ShipsToPlay.ConstructionDataStatus: See Ship_Construction; some costs depend on model gun ports

ShipsToPlay.EnglishDescription: Built at the San Martinas docks with money from the Flemish community and presented to the Crown as a gift of thanks. The old Flemish inscription survives on board: “With the help of Neptune and Boreas I cast anchor in harbor.” In Hispaniolan service, she was named Nuestra Señora del Buen Viento (“Our Lady of the Fair Wind”), and she serves as a reminder that the north wind can work for the king too.
ShipsToPlay.ConstructionDataStatus: See Ship_Construction; some costs depend on model gun ports

ShipsToPlay.EnglishDescription: A heavy galleass from the Al-Khalifa shipyards and the pride of the Khanfar Caliphate’s fleet. Four masts, a bank of oars, and multi-tiered armament make her a weapon for any situation: just as deadly in narrow straits as in open water. Her gilded stern is visible for miles–so the enemy knows who is coming.
ShipsToPlay.ConstructionDataStatus: See Ship_Construction; some costs depend on model gun ports

ShipsToPlay.EnglishDescription: The flagship frigate of the Danish navy, launched at Copenhagen in 1801. For six years she guarded Danish waters, until a British armada fell on Copenhagen in September 1807. The whole fleet was seized in a single night: a preemptive strike to keep Napoleon from getting to it first. Rota changed flags and served her captors for another eight years. A prize of war that never returned home.
ShipsToPlay.ConstructionDataStatus: See Ship_Construction; some costs depend on model gun ports

ShipsToPlay.EnglishDescription: A San Fulgencio-class ship of the line, 64 guns, launched at Ferrol in 1787. She served for more than 25 years: she fought against France, took part in the siege of Toulon (1793), and spent years on station in the Caribbean. At Trafalgar (1805), she fired on the British flagships, survived, and managed to slip away to Cadiz. She ended her service in Cuba in 1810, wrecked by storms, and finally sank in 1814.
ShipsToPlay.ConstructionDataStatus: See Ship_Construction; some costs depend on model gun ports

ShipsToPlay.EnglishDescription: An American privateer brig, purchased on April 20, 1780, by Blair McClenachan and the firm Charles Miller & Co. Based in Philadelphia. Fast, bold, greedy. She hunted British merchantmen for two years–until she became a prize herself. In 1782, she was caught by HMS Garland. A privateer lives on luck. When the luck runs out, everything runs out.
ShipsToPlay.ConstructionDataStatus: See Ship_Construction; some costs depend on model gun ports

ShipsToPlay.EnglishDescription: A ghost ship
ShipsToPlay.ConstructionDataStatus: See Ship_Construction; some costs depend on model gun ports

ShipUpgradesNew.EnglishDescription: A durability boost–a versatile upgrade

ShipUpgradesNew.EnglishDescription: Fast shot switching or a consumable activated a moment earlier can decide the battle

ShipUpgradesNew.EnglishDescription: Doesn’t apply to Mortars

ShipUpgradesNew.EnglishDescription: The enemy will see a “?” instead of the ship’s crew count, so they can’t predict the outcome of a boarding fight.

ShipUpgradesNew.EnglishDescription: Well-chosen maneuverability lets you realize the Guns' full potential when firing from both sides or in close combat
